subject: Re: read.cross warning, "Some chromosomes > 1000 cM in length"

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: read.cross warning, "Some chromosomes > 1000 cM in length"
parts:
> Could you please tell me as to why I am getting this Warning message while calling the read.cross function using the latest Rqtl version 1.29-2 (9 Dec 2013)?
>
>> library(qtl)
> Loading required package: parallel
>> radmap8 <- read.cross("csv", dir="/Users/debabrata/Data/MyData/Rqtl",
> + file="radmap8.csv", estimate.map=FALSE)
> --Read the following data:
> 176 individuals
> 613 markers
> 1 phenotypes
> --Cross type: f2
> Warning message:
> In summary.cross(cross) :
> Some chromosomes > 1000 cM in length; there may be a problem with the genetic map.
> (Perhaps it is in base pairs?)

R/qtl needs cM locations for markers; sometimes users have included base pair locations, which causes problems. If there are positions >1000, a warning message is issued.

If the data set has no marker positions, arbitrary distances are assigned. With many markers, this will result in locations that are >1000, and so you'd also get this warning.

This is a "warning" and not an "error", so you can ignore it and go on with map construction.

karl
